title: Welcome to the desk, {name}
text:
Glad to have you with us. A few house rules:

• Answer accurately first, quickly second, charmingly third.
• Customers don't leave until they're satisfied — or until you make them leave. Don't make them leave.
• Closing a chat on a customer who isn't done shows up in your ratings.

Your mentor is one message away. Use them.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: Kitchen notice
text: Whoever keeps putting empty coffee pots back on the hot plate: we have the CCTV. We are choosing mercy. For now.
from: Facilities

title: Casual Friday reminder
text: Casual Friday means smart casual. It does not mean the pyjama trousers someone wore on the video call last week.
from: HR

title: IT security reminder
text: Your password is not "Whiterock1". It was never "Whiterock1". If it is currently "Whiterock1", change it today.
from: IT Department

title: Compliance reminder
text: We give general explanations, not personalised investment advice. If a customer asks "should I buy it?", explain the concepts and the trade-offs. Keep it educational.
from: Compliance

title: A note on tone
text: Customers remember how you made them feel long after they forget the formula. Be clear, be kind, and confirm they understood before you wrap up.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: Rounding etiquette
text: Two decimals for money, sensible precision for everything else, and always say what you rounded. "About 4.6%" is fine. "4.5936128%" is not a personality.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: Units, please
text: Last week someone told a customer their loan payment was "1,073". Per month? Per year? In what currency? State your units. Every time.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: Check your work
text: The fastest way to lose a customer's trust is a confident wrong answer. Thirty seconds of checking beats thirty minutes of apology.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: Printer on floor 3
text: The printer on floor 3 is not broken. It is "thinking". Please stop kicking it.
from: Facilities

title: Cake in the break room
text: It's Priya from Treasury's birthday. There is cake. There is not enough cake. Move quickly.
from: Office Social Committee

title: Fire drill on Thursday
text: Fire drill on Thursday at 11:00. Finish your chats, then walk calmly to the car park. Do not bring the coffee machine.
from: Facilities

title: Jargon watch
text: "Leverage our synergies to optimise the liquidity runway" is not an answer. If a twelve-year-old couldn't follow your first sentence, rewrite it.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: About our VIP clients
text: VIP clients pay a premium for our time and they expect precision. Double-check numbers, answer every part, and don't make them wait.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: Use your mentor
text: You can show your mentor any conversation by typing @ and the chat number. Reviewing tough chats is how the best agents got good.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: Happy hour on the desk
text: Volume is up and management is feeling generous. Your next 3 chats pay 20% more.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: VIP appreciation week
text: We're courting some big accounts. Your next 2 VIP chats pay 30% more.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: Five-star drive
text: For the rest of the shift: earn a 5★ rating and we add a $40 bonus. Valid for your next 3 five-star chats.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: Quarter-end push
text: It's quarter end and every chat counts. Your next 5 chats pay 10% more.
from: Marcus Vane, COO

title: Pizza Friday
text: The pizza has arrived and so has the motivation. Your next chat pays 25% more.
from: Office Social Committee

title: Audit season
text: The auditors are in the building. Precision bonus: your next 2 chats pay 15% more. Please keep your desk tidy.
from: Compliance

title: Congratulations, {rankTitle}!
text: {name}, your numbers speak for themselves. You've been promoted to {rankTitle}. Tougher questions from here on, and better pay to match.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: Promotion confirmed
text: HR has processed your promotion to {rankTitle}. Your new business cards are on order. They will arrive with a typo, as is tradition.
from: HR

title: Moving up
text: Well earned, {name}. As {rankTitle} you'll get customers with harder problems. Lean on your mentor for the new material.
from: Marcus Vane, COO

title: Let's talk
text: Three rough ratings in a row, {name}. It happens to everyone. Slow down, re-read the question, answer every part, and check in with the customer before closing. Ask your mentor to review one of those chats with you.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: Quick check-in
text: Your last few chats haven't landed. Common causes: rushing, skipping parts of multi-part questions, closing too early. Take a breath. You've got this.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: Five in a row!
text: Five excellent chats in a row, {name}. Customers are talking about you, in a good way. Keep it up.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: You're on fire
text: Five straight top ratings. Here's a little something for your next two chats.
from: Marcus Vane, COO

title: Milestone reached
text: Conversations closed at Whiterock so far: {count}. Thank you for your work, {name}.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: Customers helped: {count}
text: That's {count} people who understand money a little better because of you. Keep going.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services

title: Your first VIP
text: You've just handled your first VIP client. They talk to each other, so every one of them matters. Nicely done.
from: Diane Whitfield, Head of Client Services
